alex_sales: FYI customer (Finwise) POC hitting intermittent failures when we route to PrivateLink across multiple AZs — needs quick triage.

jamie_se: Can you paste the error logs? 503s or timeouts?

alex_sales: Mostly 502/503 from the app, sometimes TCP RST. Happening after a traffic surge during load tests. Only on the path that goes through their firewall + our privatelink endpoint.

katie_netops: Are they using interface endpoints in multiple AZs or a single endpoint with cross-AZ routing?

alex_sales: They set up one interface endpoint in us-west-2a and peer VNets in other AZs. They assumed cross-AZ will just work.

sam_eng_infra: That topology can be fine, but some cloud providers tie interface endpoint IPs to AZ-local NACLs and route tables. If traffic egress preserves source IP, their firewall might be dropping flows after ephemeral port exhaustion.

jamie_se: Do we preserve client source IP in our connector for Private deployments?

sam_eng_infra: Yes by default we preserve source IP when using our onprem connector or interface endpoint path. But if they're NATing at their border, we see translated source IPs and concurrent connections look like they come from a small set of IPs — firewall state can blow up.

katie_netops: Two asks for them: 1) confirm they are not NATing multiple backend clients to a single SNAT IP before hitting the firewall, and 2) check that ephemeral port range is large enough (e.g., 1024-65535).

alex_sales: I'll ask them. They also asked whether VPC peering would avoid this.

jamie_se: Peering can help because traffic stays inside VPC routing (no interface endpoint overlay), but it depends on their network policy. Peering does not inherently fix SNAT issues — only avoiding a central proxy/NAT does.

sam_eng_infra: Also need to watch health-check ports and allowed destination port ranges. Some customers block high ephemeral ports and only allow 443/80 + a small range. If our runtime uses ephemeral ports for backend worker connections, they must allow that range or we need to enable connection pooling/keepalive.

katie_netops: Quick firewall snippet to share with them:

```
# Allow inbound from our interface endpoint IPs (example)
ALLOW TCP 443 from 198.51.100.0/26 -> app-subnet
ALLOW TCP 1024-65535 from 198.51.100.0/26 -> app-subnet
# Health checks
ALLOW TCP 8050, 9000 from 198.51.100.0/26 -> health-subnet
```

alex_sales: Good, I'll send. They also want pricing impact if we suggest switching to Dedicated peered network vs PrivateLink interface endpoints.

jamie_se: Cost tradeoffs: PrivateLink interface endpoints have per-GB data processing + endpoint hour charges; peering has no endpoint charge but could add cross-AZ data transfer costs depending on provider. Dedicated (reserved) gives predictable throughput and might reduce per-token costs at scale.

sam_eng_infra: From ops side: recommend they either expand ephemeral port range, enable connection reuse (keepalive), or place an egress NAT per AZ to avoid central NAT bottleneck. Prefer one NAT per AZ so source IPs are more distributed.

katie_netops: Also flag DNS: interface endpoints can cause DNS to resolve to AZ-local private IPs. If their app resolves the endpoint once and caches it, other AZs might try to talk to a remote AZ IP and hit an ACL. Advise using DNS with low TTL or our client-side multi-AZ resolution option.

alex_sales: Action items for Finwise: 1) confirm NAT behavior & ephemeral port range, 2) open firewall to 1024-65535 from our endpoint IPs for the POC, 3) consider per-AZ NAT or VPC peering if they want to avoid interface endpoint quirks, 4) send back traceroute + `tcpdump` snippet if problem persists.

jamie_se: If they send `tcpdump` we can check TCP resets and see if RST originates from their firewall. Example command to run on app host:

```
sudo tcpdump -nni eth0 host <our-endpoint-ip> and tcp
# capture 1000 packets
sudo tcpdump -nni eth0 host <our-endpoint-ip> and tcp -c 1000 -w /tmp/finwise.pcap
```

alex_sales: I'll relay. Anything else to add re: security questionnaire? They asked if PrivateLink meets their data residency + isolation control.

sam_eng_infra: PrivateLink gives interface-level isolation and keeps traffic on the provider backbone; peering also keeps it private but could expose broader route tables. For strict isolation and per-tenant ACLs, interface endpoints + security groups are easiest. Document that in the questionnaire.

katie_netops: Also include a note on audit/logging: we can provide flow logs and connection-level traces for the POC if they need packet-level evidence.

alex_sales: Perfect. I'll send this as a short runbook and follow up once they confirm NAT and firewall rules. :thumbsup:

alex_sales: thanks everyone — marking as in-progress with Finwise.
